logic.note: PCF8574 port expander at its I2C address driving an HD44780 in 4-bit mode (P0 RS, P1 RW, P2 EN, P3 backlight, P4-P7 D4-D7): power-up 8-bit mode, the 4-bit switch, clear, home, entry mode, display/cursor/blink control, cursor and display shift, function set (1 or 2 lines), CGRAM custom characters and DDRAM addressing with the 0x40 second line.

timing.note: Every instruction completes instantly; the busy flag always reads clear, so a sketch that sends too fast for a real LCD (no delay after clear) still works here. The cursor blinks at the HD44780 rate of about 0.4 s per phase.

analog.note: The contrast trimmer on the backpack is not modelled: text is always readable. On real modules a mis-set trimmer shows blank or solid blocks.

power.note: Draws a fixed 25 mA from VCC (backlight included) and works from 4 to 6 V. 4.7 kOhm pull-ups on SDA and SCL.

emulates: I2C address from the prop (0x20-0x27 PCF8574, 0x38-0x3F PCF8574A)
Nibble latching on the falling edge of EN, 8-bit power-up state and the switch to 4-bit
Clear, home, entry mode (increment/decrement, shift), display on/off, cursor, blink, cursor/display shift, function set
HD44780 ROM A00 for ASCII, plus ¥ → ← ° µ Ω
doesNotEmulate: Busy flag and instruction execution time (1.52 ms for clear/home)
Contrast trimmer, viewing angle and LCD response time (ghosting)
Katakana and other ROM A00 codes above 0x7F, except ° µ Ω
Backpacks with a different pin map (some use P0 = EN)
testOnRealDevice: Turn the contrast trimmer on the back until the text is readable
Check the address with an I2C scanner (0x27 or 0x3F are the common ones)
Add a short delay after lcd.clear() if your library does not wait for the busy flag
